rationale: Comprehensive cohort aggregation and systematic literature reviews demonstrate that visual impairment is documented in 18 out of 28 (64.3%) reported patients with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome (OMIM #617988). Because this frequency falls below 70%, visual abnormalities and retinal dysfunction cannot be considered an obligate clinical criterion for establishing the diagnosis, particularly in early childhood where neuro-ophthalmologic signs may either be absent, progressive, or under-evaluated without specialized electrophysiology.

evidence.text: A comprehensive literature review of 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome revealed that visual impairment was documented in 18 out of 28 individuals (64.3%), while other manifestations such as motor delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), speech disorder (24/28), intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), and skeletal problems (23/28) were more frequent.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: Delineation of GTPBP2-associated syndrome demonstrates that phenotypic features are progressive and age-related, showing that manifestations such as iron accumulation, neuropathy, and specific degenerative changes evolve over time rather than being uniformly present at earliest presentation.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.

evidence.text: OMIM phenotypic characterization classifies retinal anomalies and visual impairment as variable additional features of Jaberi-Elahi syndrome rather than universal diagnostic prerequisites.

source.quote: Additional features may include retinal anomalies, visual impairment

new_directions.question_text: Does routine specialized full-field electroretinography (ffERG) detect subclinical retinal dysfunction in GTPBP2-variant pediatric patients who lack overt visual impairment?
new_directions.rationale: Early index reports identified subclinical photoreceptor and bipolar dysfunction via electrophysiology before overt visual loss was noted, raising the possibility that clinical history alone underestimates ophthalmologic involvement.

new_directions.question_text: What is the age-dependent cumulative penetrance curve of optic atrophy and retinal degeneration across longitudinal GTPBP2 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether visual dysfunction is inherently non-penetrant in a subset of genotypes versus strictly age-dependent would refine surveillance guidelines and prognostic counseling.
